title: The districts, towns and villages of Mauritius
summary: How the island of Mauritius is divided: the nine districts, the city of Port Louis and the four towns, the 130 villages and the councils that run them, with the population of each district from Statistics Mauritius. Rodrigues and Agalega are arranged differently and are covered too.
audience: People finding their way around the island, moving to a new area, or working out which council serves an address.

facts.label: Districts
facts.detail: Port Louis, Pamplemousses, Rivière du Rempart, Flacq, Grand Port, Savanne, Plaines Wilhems, Moka and Black River. Rodrigues is counted as a separate island.

facts.label: Most populated district
facts.detail: 28.6% of the island's residents, on 196.2 km².

facts.label: Smallest and most crowded district
facts.detail: An estimated 2,663 people per km² at the end of 2025.

facts.label: City and towns
facts.detail: The city is Port Louis. The towns are Beau Bassin-Rose Hill, Quatre Bornes, Vacoas-Phoenix and Curepipe.

facts.label: Villages
facts.detail: Each elects a Village Council of 9 councillors.

facts.label: District Councils
facts.detail: Black River, Flacq, Grand Port, Moka, Pamplemousses, Rivière du Rempart and Savanne.

facts.label: Town and country
facts.detail: 481,069 residents lived in the five municipal areas and 752,028 in the villages and on Rodrigues.

facts.label: Rodrigues
facts.detail: Run by the Rodrigues Regional Assembly and divided into 6 local regions.

blocks.text: The island of Mauritius is divided into nine districts. Statistics Mauritius counts people by district, and each district has its own District Court. Local government follows a different map. It rests on one city, four towns and 130 villages, each with an elected council, and on seven District Councils that group the villages.
Rodrigues is not one of the nine districts. Statistics Mauritius lists it as a separate island, and it is run by its own Regional Assembly. Agalega has Village Committees instead of councils.

sections.heading: What are the nine districts, and how many people live in each?

blocks.text: The census figures are the residents counted on the night of 3 to 4 July 2022. The 2025 figures are estimates. They start from the census, add an allowance for young children it missed, and carry forward births, deaths and moves.

Plaines Wilhems, where four of the five municipal areas lie, holds 28.6% of the island's residents. Port Louis is the smallest district and the most densely peopled. Between the 2011 and 2022 censuses Black River grew the most, by 11,097 people, while Plaines Wilhems lost 21,512 and Port Louis 12,099.

sections.heading: Which are the city and the towns?

blocks.text: Mauritius has one city, Port Louis, and four towns: Beau Bassin-Rose Hill, Quatre Bornes, Vacoas-Phoenix and Curepipe. The city is run by a Municipal City Council and each town by a Municipal Town Council. Each is divided into wards, and every ward returns four councillors. The last municipal elections were held on 4 May 2025.

Town limits and district limits do not match. The city of Port Louis reaches into Moka and Black River districts, which is why it has more residents than Port Louis district. Quatre Bornes and Beau Bassin-Rose Hill each have a ward that extends into Black River, and one ward of Vacoas-Phoenix extends into Moka.

These five municipal areas are what the census calls urban. In 2022 they held 481,069 people, 39% of the residents of the Republic, on about 12% of its land. Between the 2011 and 2022 censuses Port Louis and Vacoas-Phoenix grew a little, while Beau Bassin-Rose Hill lost 10,949 residents, Curepipe 7,463 and Quatre Bornes 4,537.

sections.heading: How are the villages and the District Councils arranged?

blocks.text: Outside the municipal areas the island is made up of 130 villages. Each returns nine councillors to its Village Council. The last village council elections were held on 22 November 2020. Under the Act a council lasts six years from its election unless it is dissolved sooner or its life is extended, and writs for a new election are issued within 60 days of the dissolution.

Above the villages are seven District Councils. Their members are not chosen by the public directly. Within a week of a village election, the councillors of each village elect one or two of their number, by secret ballot, to sit on the District Council.

There is no District Council of Port Louis or of Plaines Wilhems. The census classes Port Louis district as wholly urban, and Plaines Wilhems is almost wholly made up of the four towns: only 6,284 of its residents were counted in village areas.

Local authorities provide services and carry out works at local level. The Ministry of Local Government lists street lighting, the building and upkeep of roads, drains and public spaces, bus shelters and traffic centres, refuse collection, markets and fairs, sports and cultural activities, and the upkeep of cemeteries and cremation grounds. The Ministry administers the Local Government Act 2011 and gives the councils general policy guidance.

The Act sets out the purpose of a local authority. It includes promoting the social, economic, environmental and cultural well-being of the local community and making sure that services are accessible and equitably distributed. The city council is led by a Lord Mayor, a town council by a Mayor, and a District Council or Village Council by a Chairperson.

sections.heading: How are Rodrigues and the outer islands run?

blocks.text: Rodrigues has no municipal, district or village councils. Its Regional Assembly holds, in Rodrigues, the powers that a Municipal Council has on the island of Mauritius, along with wider responsibilities. For its elections the island is divided into six local regions: La Ferme, Marechal, St Gabriel, Baie aux Huitres, Port Mathurin and Grande Montagne. The census treats the whole of Rodrigues as rural.

In Agalega the Local Government Act provides for Village Committees in three localities, La Fourche, Sainte Rita and Vingt Cinq, set up by the Agaléga Island Council. The islands are administered by the Outer Islands Development Corporation. For general elections Agalega forms part of constituency No. 3, Port Louis Maritime and Port Louis East.

sections.heading: Are districts the same as constituencies?

blocks.text: No. For National Assembly elections the island of Mauritius is divided into 20 constituencies, and Rodrigues forms the 21st. Their names show that they do not follow district lines: constituency No. 14 is Savanne and Black River, and No. 4 is Port Louis North and Montagne Longue.
